title: Secret Note
statement: Two friends hide notes by shifting every lowercase letter k places forward in the alphabet, wrapping from z back to a. Every other character (spaces, digits, punctuation, capital letters) stays the same. Given the note and k, return the hidden note.

answerKey.pattern: Character codes with modulo 26, building the result with an array or a string builder
keyPoints: For each character: if it is between 'a' and 'z', turn it into a number 0-25, add k, take % 26, and turn it back into a letter
Collect the characters in an array or StringBuilder and join once at the end
edgeCases: Capital letters and punctuation stay the same
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Concatenating strings in a loop: may be O(n²) because each + copies the string
Shift one step at a time, k times: O(n · k)

hints: Letters have number codes: 'a' is 97 and 'z' is 122. How could you turn a letter into a position 0-25 and back?
position = code - 97. The new position is (position + k) % 26. Reduce k first so the numbers stay small.
Strings cannot be changed in place, and += in a loop can copy the whole string each time. Push characters into an array (or a StringBuilder in Java) and join once.
